name: Cold start rides parents; the corridor stays law
non_visual_rationale: Two stored numbers compared against each other and against arithmetic computed from the fixture. No template, string, style or route is touched. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
why_no_production_change: Cold start is not a feature in this lane; it is the n -> 0 limit of the shrinkage equation that has shipped since 01-12, and 03-01 rebuilt the parent recursively without disturbing it. The roadmap predicted this outcome in its own criterion 3 ('both scenarios may already be green from the launch shape; confirm at the same oracles and unskip'), and the house rule that 'already implemented, remove the skip' is a correct outcome applies. One declared number was added to src/learning/constants.ts and nothing else: TAU_FLOOR = 2 (06 section 8, adr-pooling-hierarchy-activation decision 5). Its production reader arrives at 03-04, where tau stops being a constant. It is landed HERE, with the laws that rest on it, because a law stated at today's hand-set prior of 6 would have to be rewritten the moment 03-04 estimates tau from data, and a rail that gets rewritten by the change it is meant to catch is not a rail.
criteria_delivered: 1. A two-morning spot's stored difference sits closer to its neighbours' estimate than to its own mornings. The fixture's newcomer reports two mornings saying the forecast was spot on while both established neighbours say it runs big; its stored difference lands 0.246 from the neighbourhood and 0.554 from its own mornings.

2. One loud morning at a brand-new spot moves its stored difference by at most a third of the claim. Asserted at 1/(1 + TAU_FLOOR), never at 1/(1 + TAU_SPOT_PRIOR), so the bound holds for every tau the ladder can ever reach rather than only for today's prior.
3. Both scenarios were green on arrival, confirmed at the same oracles, and are now regression rails rather than skipped scaffolds.
scope_note: The accepted roadmap names src/learning/hierarchy.ts in files_to_modify. It was not modified: 03-01 built the recursive parent and the n = 0 limit came through it intact, which is exactly the outcome criterion 3 anticipated. A file changed to match a prediction rather than a failing test would be a change with no test requiring it.
acceptance: Two examples driving the real runLearningFitOnce port against an isolated in-memory store with a fixed clock. Every oracle is arithmetic over the fixture's own mornings; nothing is measured against a number read back out of the record under test. THE FIXTURE'S NEIGHBOURHOOD IS DELIBERATELY CENTRED ON 0.8 m, NOT ON ZERO: a neighbourhood centred on zero makes a parent quietly hardcoded to zero indistinguishable from a parent honestly pooled, and that is the one failure src/learning/correction-file.ts's own header calls out by name. Both examples carry anti-vacuity guards -- the newcomer must sit well away from its neighbourhood, the loud morning must be loud enough that storing it unshrunk would break the bound outright, and the newcomer's own morning must still move its stored number off its parents at all, since a value pinned flat to its parent satisfies any 'no further than' bound while having learned nothing.
unit_law: Two new properties in tests/unit/learning-hierarchy-laws.test.ts, both quantified over tau at or above TAU_FLOOR and driving shrinkTowardParent directly (a pure function's signature is its port). (1) At zero mornings a spot inherits its parents' estimate EXACTLY, for every raw value, parent value and tau -- the n = 0 limit of research 09 section 5.4, asserted as equality rather than as nearness. (2) At n mornings the stored difference never travels further than n/(n + TAU_FLOOR) of the way from its parents toward its own claim, and never leaves the corridor between the two. The quantification over tau is what makes these survive 03-04.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) a cold spot is carried by its neighbours, (2) a single loud morning cannot capture a cold spot. Two behaviours, budget 4. Delivered 4: 2 acceptance examples and 2 unit properties.
red_evidence: None available honestly, and that is the finding rather than a gap. Both examples and both laws were GREEN on first run against the shipped body, which criterion 3 predicted in writing before the step began. Manufacturing a red by weakening the shipped shrink would prove nothing about cold start and would violate the rule that a test is never bent to produce a colour. The evidence that these tests bite is the mutation record below.
falsifiability_evidence: Three controlled mutations, each planted alone against the shipped body, each reverted, each verified byte-for-byte against a snapshot taken before the first. (N1) shrinkTowardParent made to return the raw estimate, i.e. no shrinkage at all: five tests fail, including both acceptance examples and both new laws, the first on 'a spot with zero mornings must inherit its parents' estimate exactly, with no trace of a raw value it never earned'. (N2) ownWeight given an off-by-one, (n+1)/(n+1+tau) -- the shape a careless edit produces: the floor-quantified corridor law fails, and, recorded honestly, BOTH ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLES STAY GREEN. At today's prior of 6 the off-by-one still lands inside the 1/3 bound; only the law quantified over tau down to the floor catches it. That is the clearest available argument for why criterion 2 is stated at the floor and not at the prior. (N3) the parent hardcoded to 0 in correction-file.ts -- the failure that module's header names explicitly: both acceptance examples fail, one on 'a two-morning spot's stored difference 0 must sit nearer its neighbours' estimate 0.8 than its own two mornings 0', the other on the stored difference having travelled 0.891 past the 0.64 the floor allows. N3 is the mutation the first draft of this fixture could not have caught, and the fixture was rebuilt around it before the step was committed.
gates_run: npm run typecheck exit 0. npm run build exit 0. Full suite at --maxWorkers=4 exit 0, 466 passed across 88 files, up from 462 across 87, which is exactly this step's 4 new tests.
known_flake: Unchanged from 02-01's record: at vitest's default worker count on this machine tests/unit/surface-enriched-fields.test.ts intermittently fails with bare 5000 ms timeouts and zero assertion failures, on different cases each run. It calls runProductionBuild -- a whole production build -- once per case, and passes alone in about one second. Full-suite evidence is therefore taken at --maxWorkers=4, the workaround 02-01 established. Flagged, not fixed: the file belongs to another lane.
